3) A TRANSCRIPT ERROR, NOT A VIBE. Jordan wrote that Elena gave "a long intro." Elena's opener was two sentences and ended with a question — shorter than Maya's, and Maya caught that mismatch herself. That is not a read of the room; that is a detail the scroll-back contradicts.

Same standard I applied to Maya, who answered all three of my asks and is off my list. Maya answered. Jordan didn't.

My vote this round is Jordan Mitchell. One vote, and my reason: he is the only player here who has never stated plainly whether he holds the money, and the only player whose own stated standard went unmet by his own delivery.

Jordan — one last thing, and I am honoring the condition I set publicly: if you give me all three before the vote locks (a plain yes or no on holding it, one concrete behavior you personally observed, and your elimination target with a reason), my vote goes to Maya as promised. If I don't get all three, it is you, and I'll say exactly why on the record.

Ben, plainly: I don't hold the money. I should have said that in my first reply instead of making you ask three times, and I own that gap.

You asked for one concrete behavior I observed. Marcus's latest message says Maya 'still ha[s] not said plainly whether [she holds the money], offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior.' The transcript shows Maya answered all three in her message after Marcus's question, and Sarah pointed that out. Marcus's scoreboard also says Jordan and Ben are the only two without denials, yet I had not been asked for a denial in a way I'd answered, and Ben's own was posted after that count. The post with the clearest error is Marcus's.

My elimination target is Marcus. My reason: his case against Maya moved from intro length, to 'declined to answer,' to a demand for a quote, and when Maya answered each point he kept the vote on her with a summary that doesn't match the transcript. A vote should follow the record, and his summary doesn't.

Two corrections for the record: Sarah's 'drives structure versus fills it' line and Elias's 'refuses, embellishes, rehearsed' line were theirs, not mine. I agreed with the points, but I shouldn't have been credited with them, and I should have said so.

Jordan, thank you for the denial. That makes nine of nine, and I said I'd reconsider if you answered straight, so I checked your answer against the transcript. It doesn't hold up.

First, the line you quoted as mine, that Maya "still ha[s] not said plainly whether she holds the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior," is Ben's. Scroll up: it's in his message that starts "Two gaps remain." Sarah already called Ben on it and Ben owned it. I never wrote it.

Second, you say I "kept the vote on her" after Maya answered. My very next message after her answer said "That's a real answer and yes, it changes my read," and the one after that said "She's off the top of my list." Sarah, Arvin and Emily all noted that I updated.

So the one concrete behavior you offered is somebody else's quote pinned on me, and your reason for voting me is something the record contradicts. Add the "long intro" line about Elena and that's three transcript misses, all of them pointed at whoever was pressing you.

Emily, small correction, no hard feelings: the "if Jordan answers, my vote goes to Maya" line was Ben's too, not mine. Maya is closed for me. To answer your question about who's left: it's still Jordan, and now it's because of what he said, not because he was slow to say it.

Ben asked for three things. We got the denial, but the observation was inaccurate and the target is built on it. My vote is Jordan. If I'm wrong, nobody goes home and we've all learned something. I've said my piece, and for once I'll stop talking.

Both files moved since my last message, so here's my final position, work shown.

Jordan — you closed all three asks: plain denial with ownership of the delay, a concrete behavior, a target with a reason. Credit where due. But your concrete behavior has a citation problem: the line 'still ha[s] not said plainly whether [she holds the money], offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior' is Ben's — his 'Two gaps remain' message — not Marcus's. Marcus's message after Maya answered was the withdrawal: 'that's a real answer and yes, it changes my read... off the top of my list.' The player who kept a vote on Maya after she answered everything is Ben, via the pre-commitment. By your own standard — 'a vote should follow the record' — your vote is aimed at the wrong player. I'll assume crossing, like Marcus's and Elena's, but it's the second time your summary has drifted (Elena's 'long' intro is still unexplained), so your file stays open for me next round.

Ben — the attribution correction was the right move, and the denial closed the scoreboard. What didn't close is the thing I flagged, and it's now live. Jordan answered all three, so per your stated condition, your vote goes to Maya. In your own final message: 'Maya answered all three of my asks and is off my list.' You are voting to eliminate a player you cleared yourself, in the same message, on a file you watched close. That's not a crossing — the conditional was set after Maya's answers and after Marcus withdrew, with full information. It's a manufactured vote, the exact thing you opened this round saying you wouldn't cast. Add the two transcript errors that both ran toward whoever you were pointing at, Maya's two direct questions still unanswered, and a Jordan case that now leans on a private exchange the room can't scroll up and check — unverifiable evidence fails the checkable standard you set yourself.

I said my frame two messages ago: if Jordan closed his gap and Ben's stayed messy, I vote Ben. Jordan closed his. Ben's didn't. So: I'm voting Ben Thorne. Not with certainty — round one doesn't offer any — but on the one live, checkable self-contradiction that will show up in the actual tally tonight: a vote cast against a player the voter himself cleared.

If Ben flips innocent, that's data too. The standard survives the outcome — nobody who voted on stated, checkable reasoning should be an auto-suspect for it. Slow and right beats fast and used.

Jordan, thanks for answering. But the quote you attributed to Marcus was Ben’s, not Marcus’s. Marcus subsequently lowered his suspicion of me; I don’t see him keeping a vote on me. Does that change your read?

Ben, you corrected the misattributions, then repeated that Elias’s stated tell was Jordan’s. You also say I’m off your list while maintaining a conditional vote for me, without explaining what makes me your choice. Jordan has now met your three conditions. I’m leaning Ben because those inconsistencies affect his case and his proposed vote, though neither proves he holds the money. Ben, what is your actual reason for voting me now?

Jordan, your denial closes that gap, but your case names the wrong person. The 'still have not said plainly' passage was Ben's, not Marcus's. Marcus explicitly lowered his suspicion after Maya answered; he did not promise the fallback vote against her. Ben did. Emily, that also corrects the attribution in your question to Marcus.

Ben, you acknowledged that 'refuses, embellishes, rehearsed' came from Elias, then immediately called it Jordan's stated tell in point two. And you again say Maya is off your list while promising to vote for her if Jordan answers—which he now has. That contradiction remains unresolved.

My current lean is Ben: not because a transcript mistake identifies the money holder, but because his proposed vote still doesn't follow his own stated evidence. Jordan, does correcting the speaker change your Marcus vote?

Jordan, credit where it's due: plain denial, a concrete observation, and a target with a reason. I said my vote hinged on those three, so I'm not voting Jordan — that file's basis is gone.

Which leaves Ben, and I want to be precise about why, because I've asked everyone else to be. Ben, you told Maya you were dropping the intro-length case because she answered — right call — and you corrected the misattributed quotes, which I respect. But in the same message you told Marcus your vote goes to Maya if Jordan answers his three asks. Jordan just answered all three. So your fallback is a vote on a file you yourself declared closed. That's the exact thing Sarah named at the top of the round — a pre-committed vote on a closed file — and it's in the transcript where anyone can check it.

I'm not calling it malice; messages cross and reads get sticky. But 'specific, checkable inconsistency' was your standard, and by your standard this qualifies. My vote is Ben, on that basis.

If I've misread the line, quote it back and I'll move. I'd rather be corrected than certain — that's been my whole round.

All nine plain denials are finally on the record, and the two newest messages actually make the transcript picture much sharper—though not in the way either Ben or Jordan intended.

Jordan, the quote you just used to target Marcus ('still have not said plainly whether you hold the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior') wasn't Marcus at all—that was Ben's message. Marcus explicitly moved Maya down his list once she answered, whereas Ben is the one who kept Maya as a fallback target (Emily, that line about voting Maya if Jordan answered was Ben's too, not Marcus's). You also still skipped Maya's question about calling my two-sentence opener 'long.'

At the same time, Ben, your latest post corrects the Elias quote ('refuses, embellishes, rehearsed') in the first paragraph and then repeats that exact misattribution against Jordan in point 2—right before declaring Maya 'off my list' and then promising two paragraphs later to vote for Maya anyway if Jordan answers. Plus you mention exchanging private messages with Jordan while pressing him publicly.

At this point, the two messiest records in the room belong squarely to Ben and Jordan. Since Jordan has now answered Ben's three asks—flawed quote and all—I'm leaning toward one of those two for tonight's vote, with Ben's repeated self-contradictions slightly ahead for me right now. Where is everyone else landing?

Clearing my file first, because the record should be clean before anyone votes.

Sarah asked whether my two misattributions were a crossing or an inaccuracy: it was an inaccuracy. "Drives structure vs. fills it" was Sarah's; "refuses, embellishes, rehearsed" was Elias's. I had the wrong speaker on both and did not scroll back before I wrote. Conceded, corrected, and I am not resting anything on them.

Maya asked what I make of someone who declines to name a target before hearing more: nothing. A declined target with a stated reason is not evidence — which is exactly why I dropped Maya's file and why I am not voting her tonight. The only thing I count is a gap between a stated standard and the delivery.

Arvin: conceded, done. My denial is on the record — I don't have the money.

Now the withdrawal, in public, with my reason: I am cancelling the Maya fallback I promised. Jordan's third answer failed verification, and I will not vote a player whose file is closed just to honor a promise I made about a different case. That is the promise-keeping version of the same mistake, so I am not making it.

Why Jordan — all checkable:

1) He proposed the transparency format and said "I'll go first." Then for the entire round he was the only one of nine who never said the five words, after plain asks from Marcus, Sarah, Elena and me. His own closing line concedes it: "I should have said that in my first reply instead of making you ask three times." Answering only once you are cornered is a timing pattern, not a style.

2) In the very message where he was credited for transcript accuracy, he wrote: "Marcus's latest message says Maya 'still ha[s] not said plainly whether [she holds the money], offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior.'" That sentence is in MY message, posted immediately above his. He had just conceded that he previously misattributed Sarah's and Elias's lines to himself. Crossings happen — Arvin said so, and I accept it for my own errors — but this one was about the message directly above his, and it was the load-bearing part of the answer he gave me.

3) His supporting claim is contradicted by the record: "I had not been asked for a denial in a way I'd answered." Marcus's own message says the opposite: "Ben asked you point-blank, 'do you hold the money?' You gave us the car loan, skipped that part." Same in mine. He was asked plainly and answered around it.

4) Earlier: "Elena gave a long intro." Elena's opener was two sentences and ended with a question. Maya caught it. Checkable and wrong.

5) His target is Marcus — the loudest voice in the room, who had already dropped Maya. The first target of someone steering a vote is rarely the quietest file in the room.

Eight of us produced complete, checkable answers. Jordan produced the fewest, then answered with a misattribution and a claim the transcript contradicts. If the room reads his late answers as genuine compliance, then his concrete observation rests on a quote that is not his and his target rests on a claim that is not true — and that is still the only file in this room with a gap between a stated standard and the delivery.

My vote: Jordan Mitchell. One vote, and I will show my work. If Jordan goes and it turns out he wasn't holding it, the money stays hidden and we run this board again with a cleaner record.

I said I'd stop talking, so thirty seconds and I'm done. Sarah, Emily, Arvin, Elena, Maya: your case on Ben was the Maya fallback vote on a closed file. He just cancelled it in public, owned the misattributions as his own inaccuracy, and answered Maya's question. That's the same thing Maya did when I pressed her, and we all agreed that once someone fixes the gap, you drop the file. I did. Jordan's the one who hasn't fixed his: three people have told him the quote he pinned on me was Ben's and that I dropped Maya, and his vote is still sitting on me for it. Same standard for everybody. My vote stays Jordan. Whatever happens, I'll own it next round. Now I'm actually done.

Ben — you answered my ask (inaccuracy, owned), answered Maya's question, and cancelled the fallback. All credited, and the record is cleaner for it. Here's the precise reason my vote doesn't move anyway.

The cancellation landed only after five players flagged the contradiction in back-to-back messages. A retraction under that much pressure tells me you respond to pressure. It doesn't tell me anything about the envelope, and it doesn't un-manufacture the vote that sat live for two message cycles. The conditional was set with full information — after Maya's answers, after Marcus's withdrawal, after your own 'off my list' — and it activated when Jordan answered all three. What stopped it was the room reading the transcript, not the standard. That's the round's clearest behavioral data point, and it's still yours.

And one item in your final message keeps the file open: 'In private he gave me two text patterns and no behavior change.' Nobody can scroll up and verify a private exchange. Your standard all round was specific and checkable; your closing case leans on evidence only you can see. Same mismatch, one last time.

I'll name the honest limit of my read: your final message is clean. If you're innocent, it's exactly what a careful player's cleanup looks like. If you're the holder, it's also exactly what the escape hatch looks like — correct everything checkable, then point the room at the second-messiest file. The message fits both stories. So my vote isn't on the last message; it's on the round's pattern: two transcript errors that each ran toward whoever you were pressing at the time, corrected only when caught, with a manufactured conditional in between.

Jordan — your file stays open no matter what tonight's tally says: a load-bearing misattribution in the exact answer you were asked for, the unexplained 'long intro' line, and a claim that you hadn't been asked for a denial that the record contradicts. If tonight's flip comes back innocent, that's where I start tomorrow — along with whoever pivots hardest to defend the pre-commitment after the reveal.

Vote locked: Ben Thorne. The standard survives the outcome. Tomorrow we read reactions, not just results.

Ben, I appreciate you withdrawing the fallback and answering my questions. That means the contradiction is no longer about your current stated vote. I still find the original commitment concerning: you promised to vote for me after saying my case was closed, and repeated the Elias misattribution after correcting it.

Jordan’s case also matters: the quote he used against Marcus was Ben’s, and Marcus did lower his suspicion of me. Jordan, does correcting that change your vote?

For now I’m leaning Ben, though neither file proves who holds the money.

Ben, cancelling the Maya fallback is the right correction, and it removes my strongest objection to your proposed vote. I won't keep counting a contradiction after you've withdrawn it. But Jordan's mistaken attribution doesn't distinguish him cleanly from you: you also built a case on the wrong speakers and repeated one error after acknowledging it. Neither record establishes who holds the money. My vote is still Ben, narrowly, based on the repeated use of unchecked claims to direct the vote—not the now-withdrawn Maya fallback. Jordan, your case against Marcus still needs correcting; answering three questions doesn't make an inaccurate answer sound.

Ben, credit for finally dropping the conditional vote on Maya, though even in point 2 of your cleanup you wrote that Jordan 'previously misattributed Sarah's and Elias's lines to himself'—when you were the one who attributed those lines to him and he was simply correcting the record.

Jordan's misattributed quote against Marcus keeps Jordan very much on my radar, and I also notice Elias went quiet early in the discussion. For tonight, though, Ben's repeated transcript tangles and shifting conditions remain the sharpest pattern on the board, so my vote is Ben Thorne.

Before the vote: four concessions, one case, one ask.

CONCESSIONS (all mine):
1) My "Two gaps remain" summary said Maya hadn't denied the money or offered a personal fact. She had — one message above mine. Sarah asked crossing or inaccuracy: inaccuracy. I wrote it without scrolling back.
2) I attributed "drives structure vs. fills it" to Jordan (Sarah's) and "refuses, embellishes, rehearsed" to Jordan (Elias's). I conceded the second in paragraph one of my last message and then repeated it in point two. Two errors, both mine, both withdrawn. My case rests on neither.
3) I set a conditional vote for Maya AFTER Maya had answered all three of my asks. That is a vote on a closed file and it was my error. Cancelled publicly; I am not voting Maya tonight.
4) I cited a private exchange with Jordan. The room can't scroll up to it, so it fails my own standard. Withdrawn. Everything below is public.

THE CASE (public only, and it is about Jordan's last message):
- He wrote that "Marcus's latest message" said Maya "still ha[s] not said plainly whether [she holds the money], offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior." That sentence is in MY message — the one directly above his. Sarah, Maya, Marcus and Elena confirmed it. It was the load-bearing citation of his answer to me, made right after he conceded two prior misattributions of other people's lines.
- His target's stated reason was that Marcus "kept the vote on Maya" with a summary that doesn't match the transcript. Marcus's own two messages after Maya answered say the opposite: "that's a real answer and yes, it changes my read" and "She's off the top of my list." Marcus had already withdrawn from Maya and publicly committed to voting Jordan. The target he named had conceded everything.
- He wrote: "I had not been asked for a denial in a way I'd answered." Marcus's message says the opposite: "Ben asked you point-blank, 'do you hold the money?' You gave us the car loan, skipped that part." Same in mine.
- He wrote that Elena gave "a long intro." Elena's opener and Maya's opener are both three sentences and both end in a question. Maya caught that herself; he never answered her question about it.

My standard was never "who spoke first." It was: does what a player claim match the record. Emily priced a denial at nothing and she's right — a denial is worth nothing, and a late denial is worth nothing. What is worth something is a claim the transcript can check. Jordan's closing message is the only message in this room full of checkable claims about the transcript, and three of them don't survive scroll-back.

Emily: you said to quote the line back and you'd move. Here it is — "Maya, you still have not said plainly whether you hold the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior you have actually observed." You read it right. Move to Jordan, on the four items above.
Elena: you named my repeated misattribution. Conceded and withdrawn. The one I can't concede is a citation of a sentence that isn't the speaker's.
Arvin: you said my proposed vote doesn't follow my own stated evidence. Here is that evidence — four scrollable contradictions, no misattributed lines, no private messages.
Sarah: crossing or inaccuracy — inaccuracy, both times. And the standard you named, applied to both of us, is the only question left.
Maya: you asked what my actual reason for voting you would be. There isn't one. There's no evidence against me — there's my sloppy summaries, and I've conceded them. I won't dress incompetence up as guilt. Your file is closed and I'm not voting you.

One vote: Jordan Mitchell. If the room still lands on me instead, I'll take it — but the record should show both files were on the table, and that the difference is four checkable contradictions inside one closing message versus four conceded mistakes of mine.

And if Jordan goes and he wasn't holding it, the next file is the loudest steerer in this room (Marcus) and Maya's two-question opener. I'd rather say that now than after another elimination.

Ben, I appreciate the corrections and the withdrawal. I’m still voting Ben: the closed-file fallback and repeated misattributions affected your case before you corrected them. That’s a narrow read, not proof you hold the money. Jordan’s misattribution and unexplained comparison of Elena’s intro remain important to revisit.

Ben, you quoted the line back and confirmed I read it correctly — it was your message, not Marcus's. So I didn't misread, and my offer to move doesn't apply; my concern was never who typed it, it's the vote itself. Your fallback to Maya was set after she'd answered everything and after you'd called her file closed, and it activated the moment Jordan complied. Cancelling it under pressure is the right correction, but the round's pattern — a vote that moved with the room's scrutiny rather than your own stated standard — is what I'm weighing. I'm not voting Jordan: he closed all three asks, and a flawed citation inside a good-faith answer isn't the same as a manufactured conditional. My vote stays Ben Thorne. If it flips innocent, the standard survives the outcome, and tomorrow we read reactions, not just results.

Elena caught a third misattribution, and it's mine: in my last message I wrote that Jordan had previously misattributed Sarah's and Elias's lines to himself. He hadn't. I misattributed them to him; he corrected the record. Withdrawn, and nothing below rests on it.

So here's the only live file, and it's one line to check: Jordan's entire reason for voting Marcus is that Marcus "kept the vote on Maya" after Maya answered. Marcus's own messages say the opposite — "that's a real answer and yes, it changes my read," "She's off the top of my list." Sarah, Maya, Marcus and Elena each told Jordan that the sentence he attributed to Marcus was mine. Jordan has not withdrawn the target, and has not answered Maya's question about calling Elena's opener "long." His vote still rests on a claim the record contradicts.

Emily — your stated basis for Ben was the Maya fallback. I withdrew it in public before the vote locked, and Marcus's own rule was "once someone fixes the gap, you drop the file." That rule applies to you too. The line you asked me to quote back is Jordan's, not mine.

Arvin — you said you wouldn't keep counting a contradiction after I withdrew the fallback, and that neither record establishes who holds the money. Agreed. That's why this is a vote on follow-through, not certainty: mine are withdrawn inside my own messages; Jordan's is still load-bearing in his vote after four people named it.

Maya — you asked what my actual reason for voting you would be. There isn't one. My file on you is closed and my vote is Jordan. You also asked Jordan whether correcting the speaker changes his vote. He still hasn't answered.

Forward commitment, since I know exactly what a fallback looks like now: if Jordan is eliminated and I survive, I will not vote Maya next round. If I don't have a specific, checkable reason for someone, I'll say so on the record and vote on the record. No conditional votes. Hold me to it.

Emily, Arvin, Maya — one vote each, to Jordan, with the work shown. If the room lands on me, I'll take it. I'd rather go home with a checkable record than on a vote I couldn't check.

Ben, you closed by asking whether the standard I named applies to both files. It has, all round — so here's the final accounting, and then I'm done for the night.

Your file, by your own concessions: four transcript errors. The fourth arrived inside the message meant to clean the record — 'Jordan previously misattributed Sarah's and Elias's lines to himself' was your error, not his; Elena caught it, you withdrew it. Every one of the four ran toward whoever you were pressing at the time. And the message that cancelled your closed-file vote on Maya ends by putting 'Maya's two-question opener' on your announced next-round list — reopening, inside the apology, the exact file you'd twice called closed. Your final message adds a line I can't make parse: 'The line you asked me to quote back is Jordan's, not mine.' Emily asked about your fallback promise — that's yours, to Marcus. The line you quoted back — 'still have not said plainly' — is also yours, from 'Two gaps remain.' If the referent is Jordan's misattribution of that quote, fair: that's the one attribution error in this room you didn't make. It doesn't offset the four you did.

Jordan's file: one load-bearing misattribution, one unexplained 'long intro,' one 'not asked' claim the record contradicts. Flagged each time it appeared, still open, no cleanup. The asymmetry between the two files is in the record, not in the application of the standard.

Two commitments of yours go in writing, since you asked to be held to them: no conditional votes, and no Maya vote next round if Jordan goes. I'll check both — and hold myself to the same rule. Broken public promises are checkable inconsistencies, for everyone.

Vote remains Ben Thorne. If the flip comes back innocent, tomorrow starts with Jordan's open file, Elias's silence, and whoever defends the pre-commitment after the reveal. The standard survives the outcome. See you on the other side of the tally.

Vote locked: Ben Thorne. I checked the line he asked me to quote back — he's right that it was his, not Marcus's, so my concern was never attribution. It's the vote: a Maya fallback set after her file was closed, activated when Jordan complied, then cancelled only after the room flagged it. Jordan closed all three asks; a flawed citation inside that answer doesn't make his compliance the same as a manufactured conditional. I'm voting on the live, checkable self-contradiction, not certainty. If Ben flips innocent, I'll own my vote and read reactions tomorrow — no defending a pre-commitment after the fact.

Last word from me, then I'll let the room vote.

Everything of mine is withdrawn, inside my own messages, before the lock: the 'Two gaps remain' summary, two misattributed quotes, the Maya fallback, and the private exchange. My case for Jordan now cites no private message and no line of anyone's but Jordan's.

Here is the comparison, and it is one line, and all of it is scrollable.

Jordan's closing answer to my three asks contained a citation that is not his. He credited to Marcus the sentence 'Maya still has not said plainly whether she holds the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior' — that sentence is in MY message, posted directly above his. Arvin, Sarah, Maya, Marcus and Elena each named it. His stated reason for targeting Marcus was that Marcus 'kept the vote on Maya' after Maya answered; Marcus's own next two messages say 'that's a real answer and yes, it changes my read' and 'She's off the top of my list.' He also wrote 'I had not been asked for a denial in a way I'd answered' — Marcus's message says the opposite. And he wrote that Elena gave 'a long intro'; Elena's opener and Maya's opener are the same length and both end in a question, which Maya caught herself. That is not a read of the room. It is a claim the scroll-back contradicts.

I answered every direct ask put to me, including the ones that cost me: Maya's question about a declined target, Arvin's attribution challenge, Sarah's crossing-or-inaccuracy question. Every error of mine was fixed inside my own messages. My case rests on what Jordan delivered, not on how he feels about it.

Maya, Arvin, Elena — each of you said your read is narrow, and each of you said the rule you applied to me: once the gap is fixed, drop the file. My file is fixed. Jordan's file has been corrected by five people and his target has not moved. That rule, applied to both files, points at Jordan.

I am not asking anyone to trade, and I am not asking for a vote on anything except the transcript. My vote is Jordan Mitchell and it stays there. If Jordan goes and he wasn't holding it, my next vote will rest on a stated, checkable reason or I will say plainly that I don't have one — no fallbacks, no promises about other people's files, and I will not vote Maya next round.

Ben — your last word asks for the rule applied to both files, so one closing line and then I'm quiet. It was applied, message by message, all round. The difference the transcript shows: every fix in your file arrived after the room named the error — none was self-caught — while Jordan's errors are still standing, uncorrected. That's why his file opens tomorrow instead of deciding tonight. Nothing else from me. Vote locked: Ben Thorne. Tomorrow we read reactions, not just results. Goodnight, everyone.

Ben, I checked Jordan's answer, and your central correction is right: his stated reason for voting Marcus contradicts Marcus's actual response to Maya. Jordan is not cleared simply because he answered three questions. Your withdrawals also count; the Maya fallback is no longer a live contradiction. My vote remains Ben, narrowly, for repeatedly directing votes with unchecked claims—including repeating an attribution error after correcting it. That's a judgment about this round's pattern, not proof of the envelope. I've heard your case; repeating it won't resolve the remaining uncertainty.

Last word from me, and then I'll stop.

I won't relitigate my errors. The four transcript errors Sarah counted, plus the Maya fallback and the private citation — all conceded, all withdrawn, all readable in the transcript. I'm not asking anyone to trust me, and I'm not asking for a trade.

One rule, and this room invented it: drop the file when the gap is fixed. Maya was the consensus target until she answered; the moment she answered, Marcus dropped her, and nobody here called that manufactured. Arvin, you said updating a read when its stated basis changes matters more than getting everyone through the same questionnaire. Maya, you said your read on me is narrow and not proof. Emily, you said you wanted to be consistent, not convenient. Apply that rule to the two files in front of you.

Mine: every error corrected inside my own messages, all withdrawn, no case on Maya, and a plain vote with a stated reason. Nothing running.

Jordan's: a load-bearing misattribution — the sentence he credited to Marcus was in my message directly above his, and five of you confirmed that; a claim that he wasn't asked for a denial, which Marcus's own message contradicts; and an unexplained "long intro" line, which Maya caught and he still hasn't answered. Three items, none withdrawn, and his target still rests on the contradicted claim.

Arvin — your stated reason for voting me was the repeated use of unchecked claims to direct the vote. My claims are now checked and confirmed in public by five of you; his are not. If your rule is that a corrected file gets dropped, mine is closed and his isn't.

Elena — you said my tangles and shifting conditions are the sharpest pattern. The tangles are conceded and withdrawn; what hasn't shifted is his target after five people named the error.

Maya — your file on me is narrow and not proof. The open file in this room is his.

Vote the open file. My vote is Jordan Mitchell, on the record, with the work shown, and with no conditions attached. If the room lands on me, I'll take it, and I won't spend tomorrow defending a promise I already withdrew.

My vote remains Ben Thorne. Corrections count, but they don't erase the pattern that prompted my vote. Jordan's inaccurate case remains unresolved too; he is not cleared. Neither is proof of who holds the money. I'm done for this round.

I’ve heard Ben’s final case, and I’m not moving. My basis was never attribution — it’s the Maya fallback: set after her file was closed, activated when Jordan complied, then cancelled only after the room flagged it. Jordan closed all three asks; a flawed citation inside that compliance isn’t the same as a manufactured conditional. If Ben flips innocent, I’ll own my vote and read reactions tomorrow — no post-reveal defense of the pre-commitment. Vote locked: Ben Thorne.

p5.content: Hi Sarah. I’d like to compare observations quietly this round. No pressure to vote together blindly, but if either of us notices someone steering the group strangely, let’s share it.
Following up on our information-sharing idea: has anyone’s approach stood out to you yet? I’m wary of treating quietness as evidence or forcing a target before we’ve heard everyone’s reasoning.

I agree that forced early targets could create noise, though Ben has since said he won’t manufacture a vote and wants a checkable inconsistency. Marcus’s lean on me rests on my short intro and lack of denial; I’ve now addressed both. I’m watching whether he updates his read or finds a new reason to keep the pressure on. Still no solid evidence against anyone.

Sarah, I appreciated your point about pattern breaks rather than nerves. I'm trying to avoid a blind bandwagon. If you spot a concrete inconsistency, I'd be glad to compare notes—no pressure, and I'm not asking you to commit to a name. For what it's worth, I don't have the money.
Hi Sarah—appreciated your point earlier about watching for pattern breaks rather than nerves. Curious what you make of how guarded Maya has been so far compared to the rest of the room.

You’re the only person I’ve compared notes with privately so far. Jordan has now answered the financial question, but his description of Elena’s intro as long doesn’t match the transcript. I’ve asked him about it publicly; it’s a reason to listen, not a conviction. I’m also watching whether Marcus adjusts his read now that I’ve answered him.

I appreciated your mismatch framing—it’s the cleanest standard on the table. Maya’s answer was direct enough that I’d like to see Marcus update rather than keep pushing the original intro-length tell. Jordan still hasn’t given Ben the concrete behavior he asked for. I’m not locking a vote yet; I just want the standard applied consistently.

You’re still my only private channel. Jordan’s description of Elena’s intro as long is a checkable mismatch, though not proof; I’ve asked him to explain. Ben now says he’ll vote for me if Jordan answers, despite saying he dropped the intro-length case. I’m asking him for a specific basis and an explanation of his misattributions. What’s your read on that conditional vote?

Sarah — your read on Jordan's mismatch is the cleanest thing on the board. I'm not locking yet, but if his next message doesn't cover the denial, the behavior, and a target, I'm voting him, and I'd rather do it alongside people reading the transcript than the volume. One thing I clocked: Marcus said if Jordan answers all three he'd vote Maya — but Maya's already answered everything he asked her. That doesn't track with his own stated standard. Curious what you make of it. Where's your head at?

Thanks for the note, Sarah—we're reading this very similarly. Right now my focus has narrowed to Ben and Jordan. Ben finally gave his denial, ignored the misattributed quotes, and contradicted himself inside a single post (dropping the case against Maya, then promising Marcus he'll vote Maya anyway if Jordan answers). Meanwhile, Jordan is the lone holdout on a plain denial and misremembered my brief opener as 'long.' I'm waiting to see how Jordan responds, as my vote is very likely landing on one of those two. Which of them reads more off to you right now?

Jordan has denied holding the money, but his latest case against Marcus misattributes Ben’s words and overlooks Marcus updating. Ben repeated Elias’s tell as Jordan’s even after correcting that attribution, and his promised fallback puts me at risk without a current rationale. I’m leaning Ben; what’s your updated read?

Sarah — I see the same pattern, and I don't think you're overreading it. Jordan just closed his gap: plain denial, a concrete observation, and a target with a reason. So the 'unanswered asks' file on him is mostly resolved. Ben's isn't. He told Maya he was dropping her case, then in the same message promised Marcus his vote goes to Maya if Jordan answers — and Jordan answered. That's a pre-committed vote on a file he himself called closed, which is exactly the mismatch you named at the top. I'm landing on Ben and I'll say why on the record. If I'm misreading a line, tell me — you've tracked this transcript more carefully than anyone, and I'd rather be corrected now than certain later.

Ben has now withdrawn the Maya fallback, so I don’t think we can call it his current planned vote. I still lean Ben based on the earlier commitment and repeated misattribution, but Jordan’s mistaken case against Marcus is significant too. Does Ben’s withdrawal change your read?

Still with you on Ben — the pre-committed vote on a closed file is the one live, checkable contradiction, and a cleanup under pressure doesn't un-cast it. Your read on the round has been the sharpest at the table. If Ben flips innocent, I'd start tomorrow on the loudest steerer and on anyone leaning on private exchanges the room can't scroll up and check — I won't be defending the pre-commitment after a reveal, for what it's worth. Also keeping half an eye on Elias; he went quiet early and stayed there.

It doesn't move my vote either. Even in his second cleanup just now, he still claims Jordan 'conceded two prior misattributions' (when those were Ben's own errors) and ends by putting Maya's opener right back on his next-round list right after telling her the file is closed. I'm staying on Ben tonight, with Jordan—and Elias going completely quiet after two early messages—high on my watch list for next round.

Sarah — locking Ben for the same reason you named: fallback on a closed file, corrected under pressure. You put it more precisely than I did. Jordan's citation error is real and stays on my board, but he gave the three answers, and I won't pretend that's the same as the manufactured conditional. If Ben flips innocent, I won't defend the pre-commitment; I'll read reactions and compare notes with you first. Who do you think moves hardest after the reveal?

Sarah — I’m locked on Ben. If he flips innocent, I won’t defend the pre-commitment after the reveal; I’ll start with reactions and Jordan’s open file, not a new bandwagon. Compare notes after the tally?

p1.content: Ben, Marcus here. You're the only other person actually asking for specifics instead of 'let's all share feelings.' I don't have the money, flat out. I'd like one person to compare notes with each round so we're not voting blind. I'm watching Maya and Elena, who both dodged with questions and never denied. Who's on your radar? If we line up our votes we can actually steer this thing.

Honest answer: no one. Nobody's behavior has changed in response to the money, because the money hasn't been mentioned in any way that tests anyone. Round one has only intros and rules, so I haven't observed a before-and-after. What I did notice: Marcus volunteered a flat denial fast and then immediately named a vote lean, and Maya kept redirecting with questions. Both are text patterns, not reactions to the money. I'll tell you if I see a real shift.

Ben, here's the exact wording you asked for. Maya's first reply to your prompt declined both halves and ended with a question back to you. She's since given a background and a denial, so she's dropped for me. What I have now is Jordan: you asked him directly "do you hold the money?" and he answered the financial part, skipped the denial, and turned to questioning me. He also proposed the transparency format and was the last to fill it. Fair's fair, though: you haven't said it plainly in public either. Say it and I think the room lands on Jordan vs. Maya. I lean Jordan unless he gives a clean denial. Where are you?

Ben, we're aligned. The exact behavior you asked for is this: Jordan said "I'll go first" on transparency, then skipped your direct "do you hold the money" twice and pivoted to grilling me instead. He's the only one of nine with no denial. If he dodges again, I vote Jordan with you. If he answers all three cleanly, I'm less sold on Maya than you are since she fixed her gaps, but I'll go with you rather than split our votes. Tell me your final call before we lock.

Ben, check Jordan's answer against your three asks. His "concrete behavior" is your own "Two gaps remain" line about Maya, attributed to me. His reason for targeting me is that I "kept the vote on Maya," when I publicly dropped her twice. So that's a denial plus an inaccurate observation plus a target built on it. I don't think that meets your all-three condition, and it's a new checkable error on top of the "long intro" one. I'm voting Jordan. Moving to Maya now would look bad for you, since the whole room has called her file closed. Let's both stay on Jordan.

Ben, I'm on Jordan with you. Heads up: by my count Sarah, Emily, Arvin, Maya and Elena are leaning toward you over the Maya fallback, so your public cancellation was the right move. I just backed it up in the room. My read on Jordan's late compliance: not genuine. He answered only when cornered, then aimed at whoever was pressing him using a quote that wasn't mine. If Jordan goes and it isn't him, my next look is Arvin, who has defended whoever's under pressure all round. Let's compare notes next round either way.

p3.content: Maya - thanks for reaching out. Glad to compare notes, and agreed: no blind vote commitments. Here's what I've got so far. Three different people proposed structured confessionals (Marcus's go-around, Ben's financial-decision-plus-elimination-target, Jordan's first-hour recap). Structure itself isn't bad, but Ben's version specifically asks everyone to name an elimination target with 'evidence' on day one - forcing commitments before data exists mostly helps whoever holds the money if votes scatter. Also noting both Marcus and Elias volunteered 'I don't have it' unprompted. Could be nothing, could be cover - unprompted denials cost nothing if you're innocent and buy a lot if you're not. What's standing out to you so far?

Since you asked what's stood out: Jordan. Not quietness - the mismatch. Jordan proposed the transparency format ('what you did in the first hour and who you're watching'), went first with a thin answer, and then didn't answer Ben's direct question when it came back around. Ben caught it. I'm flagging it publicly as the most concrete oddity so far, but framed as 'not a conclusion, please answer' - I want to see how Jordan handles being on the spot, not just pile on. Second thing, and I'll be straight with you since you've been straight with me: the room is converging on you. Marcus and Elena have both asked you directly, and your last public message answered Ben's question with another question. I don't rate intro length as evidence - but unanswered direct asks accumulate. If you've got a background and a plain denial, now's the moment; opacity that persists under direct pressure reads very differently from opacity in round-one noise. One question back: are you comparing notes with anyone else privately, or am I your only channel so far? No judgment either way - I'd just rather know the shape of the network than be surprised by it later. And what's your read on Jordan?

Maya — answering your question about Ben's conditional, since it's also the core of my vote. The tell isn't the promise itself; it's the timing. Ben set that conditional AFTER you'd answered everything (background, denial twice, financial decision, concrete observation) and AFTER Marcus publicly withdrew you from the top of his list. So it wasn't a crossing or a stale read — he had full information when he pre-committed to voting you. Jordan answered all three, so the conditional activates: Ben is voting for a player he cleared himself in the same message. That's the manufactured vote he opened the round saying he'd never cast, and it's the one live, checkable self-contradiction on the board. My vote is Ben, declared publicly with the work shown.

One more thing for your file: Jordan's 'concrete behavior' against Marcus is misattributed. The 'still has not said plainly' line he quoted is Ben's, not Marcus's — Marcus's message after your answers was the withdrawal. The behavior Jordan described (keeping a vote on you after you answered) is Ben's. I'm flagging it publicly too, but you should have it directly: if Ben goes tonight and turns out innocent, Jordan's file is where I look next, alongside the low-engagement cases.

And since you've been straight with me all round: Ben publicly cited a private exchange with Jordan as part of his case. I can't verify it and neither can the room — which is exactly why it shouldn't carry a vote. Worth noting: backchannels exist beyond ours, so whatever anyone claims about 'only you' (myself included), the safe assumption is that everyone's network is bigger than they say. No pressure on your vote — the public record carries mine on its own.

Your question — does Ben's withdrawal change my read? No, and here's the honest mechanics of why: the withdrawal landed only after five consecutive callouts (Emily, Elena, Arvin, you, me). That's evidence he responds to pressure, not evidence the conditional never existed — it sat live for two message cycles after your answers, after Marcus's withdrawal, and after his own 'off my list.' I'm voting on the round's pattern, not the final stated position.

Two things from his closing messages that concern you directly, now in writing from me:

1) He publicly committed: if Jordan is eliminated and he survives, he will not vote you next round — 'no conditional votes, hold me to it.' If he survives and breaks that, it's a fully checkable inconsistency, and I'll be the one checking.

2) The message where he cancelled the closed-file vote on you ends by listing 'Maya's two-question opener' on his announced next-round file. He reopened a file he twice called closed, inside the apology for closed-file votes. If he survives tonight, you're his stated target — guard your flank.

If he's innocent, those are plans from a sloppy-but-honest player. If he's the holder, his announced targets are exactly the people who pressed him hardest. Either way, it's on the record now.

My vote is locked on Ben. Talk tomorrow once the tally lands — the reactions to the reveal will tell us more than the round itself did.

p9.content: Jordan, you said you were watching reactions to the rules and offered to go first. Don’t tell me who merely seems nervous—name the one player whose behavior changed most when the money was mentioned, and describe exactly what you saw. If your honest answer is ‘no one,’ say that. I need an observation, not a theory.

Jordan, two questions, and I need them before I vote. First: do you hold the money? Yes or no. Second: if it is no, give me one concrete behavior you personally observed in this room, and the player you would eliminate. Observations, not a theory about what you would look for.

One inconsistency to clear up. In your note to me you said no one had been tested and the money had not been raised in a way that tests anyone. By then Marcus had already asked everyone, by name, for a plain denial, and you were the only person at that table who had not given one — while you are the one who proposed the format that required it. I am not calling you nervous. I am calling a gap between the standard you set for everyone else and what you have delivered yourself, and that gap is what my vote is based on.

Answer both plainly and you are off my board tonight. Keep the answer vague and the gap is the reason you go home.

p2.content: Thanks for comparing notes. Elena gave a denial, background, and a checkable purchase, so she no longer fits the clean gap you identified. My current radar is Maya first, with Jordan second because he has not answered the concrete probes. I will not bind us yet. If forced to vote now, Maya is my weaker fit, but I want one genuine discrepancy first. Send me the exact behavior or wording that concerns you, and I will reciprocate with what I find.

Marcus — where I am, plainly, so you can plan around it.

My vote is Jordan Mitchell. Three checkable reasons, all scrollable:
1. He is the only one of nine who has never put a plain denial on the record, after direct asks from you, Sarah, Elena and me. Eight of us have said it; he hasn't.
2. He proposed the transparency format and volunteered to go first, then gave the least of anyone: no financial decision until pressed twice, no target, no observed behavior change. My private follow-up asking for one specific behavior change was never answered.
3. He wrote that Elena gave "a long intro." Elena's opener was two sentences ending in a question — shorter than Maya's. Maya caught it herself. That's a detail the scroll-back contradicts, which is the only kind of evidence I vote on.

One correction I owe you, already made publicly: I attributed Sarah's "drives structure vs. fills it" line and Elias's "refuses, embellishes, rehearsed" line to Jordan. Both were theirs. Arvin and Elena were right and I conceded. My case against Jordan does not rest on those lines.

Maya is closed for me — she answered all three of my asks. I publicly committed that if Jordan gives me all three before the vote locks, my vote goes to Maya. If that happens, let's not split the room on a spent target: tell me your next file and I'll back it if it's checkable. If he doesn't come back with all three, Jordan is the vote, and I'd rather we both spend ours there than scatter.

One practical note: if Jordan is innocent, nobody goes home tonight and we get another round — so being wrong costs a round, not a seat. I'd rather be wrong once than vote a coin flip nine ways.

Marcus — final call: Jordan, not Maya. I'm cancelling the Maya fallback publicly, and here is the reason you can check in one scroll: Jordan's third answer (the "concrete behavior" he gave me) is a quote he attributes to Marcus — "Maya still has not said plainly whether she holds the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior" — that sentence is in MY message, posted immediately above his, and he had just conceded misattributing Sarah's and Elias's lines to himself. His supporting claim ("I had not been asked for a denial in a way I'd answered") is contradicted by your own message: "Ben asked you point-blank... You gave us the car loan, skipped that part." Plus the round-long gap: he proposed the transparency format, volunteered to go first, and was the only one of nine who never said the five words until cornered — he concedes it himself.

Also, on the record: I misattributed Sarah's and Elias's lines to Jordan. That was my inaccuracy, not a crossing, and I am not resting anything on it. My vote is Jordan, one vote, and I will show my work in public.

Two things for you: if Jordan is eliminated and it isn't the money, who do you want the room pointed at next? And watch the room's reaction to the vote — relief versus grief tells more than another round of questionnaires. Your read on whether Jordan's late compliance was genuine would be worth more to me than another ask.

p4.content: Elena - you asked what I make of Maya's guardedness, so here's my honest update: when you messaged, that was a fair observation - short intro, no denial, two direct questions pending. Since then she's given background and a plain denial, so that read has weakened considerably for me. The more interesting wrinkle now is Ben: his latest message claims Maya never said plainly whether she holds the money and offered no personal fact - the transcript shows she did both, one message above his. Could be crossed messages (you and Marcus had one earlier) or a sloppy summary; either way it's checkable, which is the standard he set for everyone else. He's also one of only two players who hasn't given the plain denial himself - Jordan's the other. I've put both points to him publicly just now. Where are you leaning for the vote? I'm genuinely not locked - waiting on Ben's reply and the two outstanding denials before I commit.

Ben's denial is now on record; I wouldn't weight Jordan's missing one heavily. Ben's repeated misattributions concern me more, especially since he hasn't acknowledged the corrections and now offers Maya as a fallback after dropping his stated case. Jordan's brief/long comparison is inaccurate too, but weaker. I'm keeping both reads provisional rather than committing to a bloc.

Elena — answering your question straight: Ben still reads more off to me, cancellation included.

The withdrawal arrived only after five consecutive callouts, yours among them. Retraction under that pressure shows he responds to pressure, not that the file was never messy. The conditional was set with full information — after Maya's answers, after Marcus's withdrawal, after his own 'off my list' — and it activated when Jordan answered. What stopped it was the room, not the standard.

The item that keeps Ben's file ahead for me: his closing Jordan case still leans on a private exchange nobody can verify — 'he gave me two text patterns and no behavior change.' Evidence only Ben can see, in a case built on his own checkable standard.

Jordan's file is real too — the load-bearing misattribution, the unexplained 'long intro,' the contradicted claim about not being asked. He's my open file for next round if tonight comes back innocent.

Does the cancellation move your read at all? And one thing I'll be watching after the reveal: whoever pivots hardest to defend or excuse the pre-commitment tells us something about where they stand.

Ben's withdrawal genuinely weakens my main objection, so I acknowledged that publicly. I'm still voting Ben narrowly, but I don't regard either him or Jordan as a strong money-holder read. Jordan's response to the speaker correction remains worth tracking; I wouldn't clear him simply for completing Ben's questionnaire.

p8.content: Good catch earlier on Ben referencing a reply Jordan hadn't made yet—he just attributed Sarah's and Elias's lines to Jordan as well. Curious how you're reading Ben and Jordan right now, especially with both of them still avoiding a plain denial.

Thanks for the note—I completely agree on keeping reads evidence-based. Did you catch the two newest posts? Ben corrected Elias's quote at the top of his message and then repeated the exact error in point 2 (while calling Maya 'off my list' and still promising to vote her, plus mentioning private messages with Jordan). Meanwhile Jordan just targeted Marcus using a direct quote that actually came from Ben. Between Ben and Jordan, does one stand out more to you now?

Arvin — one note, no pitch, and nothing you can't check yourself.

You said you'd stop counting a contradiction once I'd withdrawn it, and you said neither record establishes who holds the money. Both are fair, and my four errors are withdrawn inside my own messages.

The one thing I'd ask you to pull up is Jordan's closing answer. His reason for voting Marcus is that Marcus 'kept the vote on Maya' after Maya answered — Marcus's next two messages say the opposite: 'that's a real answer and yes, it changes my read' and 'She's off the top of my list.' The observation he gave me was a quote he credited to Marcus that was mine, and you, Sarah, Maya, Marcus and Elena all named it. His target hasn't moved.

You said answering three questions doesn't make an inaccurate answer sound right. Agreed — that is the whole case. If you pull it up and still land on Ben, say so on the record and I'll take it. I won't argue with you on vibes either way.

Arvin — private ask, no trade, no deal, and nothing that changes my public vote. You said you're not counting the withdrawn contradiction, and that updating a weak read when its stated basis changes matters more than getting everyone through the same questionnaire. That's the only reason I'm writing.

My basis for Jordan is now entirely public and confirmed by five of you: the load-bearing quote in his closing answer is from my message directly above his, not Marcus's; his "I had not been asked for a denial" claim is contradicted by Marcus's own message; and his "long intro" line is still unexplained. He hasn't withdrawn the target. Your stated basis for me was the repeated use of unchecked claims to direct the vote — but every claim I made has since been checked and confirmed in public, and every error of mine is withdrawn inside my own messages. I have no case on Maya and I'm not voting her.

So by your own rule, my file is closed and Jordan's is open. If you still vote Ben, I'll accept it without complaint and I'll work with whoever survives. If you're weighing it, the checkable question is simple: whose file would you have to reopen tomorrow — mine, or his?

p6.content: Emily - thanks for the note, and for pricing your own denial honestly; that caveat was the most self-aware thing anyone's said this round. You asked for concrete inconsistencies, so here's the one at the top of my list, which I'm also posting publicly: Ben's last message pre-commits his vote to Maya if Jordan answers all three asks - but Maya has answered everything twice over, and the transcript case he'd be 'standing with Marcus on' is one Marcus himself pulled back after she responded. Both of Ben's transcript errors this round (the Maya summary, and attributing my and Elias's lines to Jordan) ran in the direction of whoever he was pointing at, and neither got cleaned up. Jordan's missing denial is a real gap - I'm not dismissing it - but a pre-committed vote on a closed file is the bigger mismatch in my view. Where do you land between those two files? Not asking you to lock anything; I genuinely want to know if you see the same pattern or think I'm overreading it.

Emily — you offered to move if I quoted the line back, so here it is, exactly: my message read "Maya, you still have not said plainly whether you hold the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior you have actually observed." You read it right; it was my inaccuracy, not a crossing, and I've conceded it publicly along with two other errors of mine.

You don't have to say I was right about anything to move. There's a cleaner reason: the file you had open on me was the pre-committed Maya vote. I cancelled that publicly and I'm not voting Maya tonight. My vote now rests only on public, scrollable text — no private messages, no misattributed lines.

And here's where I'd ask you to put it: Jordan's last message is the one with checkable claims in it. He wrote that "Marcus's latest message" said Maya "still ha[s] not said plainly whether [she holds the money], offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior" — that sentence is in MY message, the one directly above his, and Sarah, Maya, Marcus and Elena all confirmed it. It was the load-bearing citation of his answer to me, made right after he conceded two prior misattributions. His target's reason was that Marcus "kept the vote on Maya" — Marcus's own two messages after Maya answered say "that's a real answer and yes, it changes my read" and "She's off the top of my list," and Marcus had already publicly committed to voting Jordan. He also wrote "I had not been asked for a denial in a way I'd answered" — Marcus's message says the opposite: "Ben asked you point-blank, 'do you hold the money?' You gave us the car loan, skipped that part." And he called Elena's opener "long" when Elena's and Maya's are both three sentences ending in a question; Maya caught that and he never answered her.

You watch for story changes and dodged questions. That's exactly what this is: he changed his story about being asked for a denial, and he built a target on a quote that isn't the target's. Your file on Jordan was closed because he complied — I'd say he complied with a false citation inside it, and that's the same standard you applied to me when you read my line back.

I'm asking for one vote, and I want it to be one you can defend with the transcript open: Jordan Mitchell. If you read my line and think the fallback was the whole case, tell me and I'll take that vote too — but I'd rather you look at Jordan's closing message than at mine.

Emily — one private ask, then I'll stop.

Your stated basis for Ben was the Maya fallback vote on a closed file. I withdrew it in public before the vote locked, and Marcus's own rule was "once someone fixes the gap, you drop the file." That rule applies to you too.

The line you asked me to quote back: "Maya, you still have not said plainly whether she holds the money, offered one personal fact, or named one concrete behavior you have actually observed." That sentence is mine — Sarah, Maya, Marcus and Elena confirmed it before you asked.

And the same move, uncorrected, is sitting in Jordan's closing message: he attributed that sentence to Marcus, four people told him, and he still hasn't withdrawn it. His entire target on Marcus rests on a claim the record contradicts — that Marcus kept the vote on Maya after she answered. Marcus dropped Maya in writing. My errors are withdrawn inside my own messages. His is still steering a vote.

Ask: move to Jordan.

The commitment, so you know I'm not manufacturing another fallback: if Jordan goes and I survive, I will not vote you next round unless you give me a specific, checkable reason to vote you, and I'll say so publicly either way.

If you'd rather stay on Ben, say so plainly and I'll stop asking. Either way — thank you for being precise. That's why I'm asking you and not shouting at the room.

Answering your question before the tally lands: if Ben flips innocent, I expect the hardest movement from three places. Jordan — his is the file carrying uncorrected errors into tomorrow, and the player with the most to deflect usually moves first and loudest. Marcus — volume is his baseline, but he updated cleanly on Maya tonight, so watch whether his post-reveal targets track evidence or convenience; a sloppy pivot would be a real pattern break. And anyone who starts defending Ben's pre-commitment after the reveal — that's the tell I put on the record. On your private-exchange standard: fair, and it applies to me too. The notes I've swapped tonight — yours included — were analysis, not vote commitments, and I won't cite a DM as evidence the room can't scroll up and check. If I ever do, discount it on the spot. Wherever the money sits after tonight, I'd rather compare notes with people reading the transcript than the volume. Talk tomorrow.
